# lnurlcash-kotlin

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer notes for Kotlin and the JVM, over the Rust core
lnurlcash-core via UniFFI. MIT.

implementation("com.lnurlcash:lnurlcash-kotlin:0.1.1")

## CRITICAL: HTTP retries

Every LNURLcash mutation (rotate/split/merge/melt) is an HTTP GET, but is NOT
idempotent - the first attempt burns the input note. A client that retries a
GET on connection failure will get "already spent" for the second attempt and
report a DEFINITIVE rejection, so the caller discards the fresh secret that was
the only copy of the note the service just minted.

java.net.http.HttpClient does this and cannot be configured out of it. This
library uses OkHttp with retryOnConnectionFailure(false). A caller-supplied
client MUST disable retries.

LUD-25 closed this at the service end: a service MUST answer a byte-identical
retried rotate/split/merge with the success it already returned, sig and all.
So the client re-sends a mutation whose answer was lost, on purpose and bounded
(LnurlcashClient(mutationRetries = N), default 1), and a dropped connection
usually resolves into Confirmed. NEVER a melt: it carries pr, is paid
asynchronously and has no replay guarantee. Never a definitive refusal. The
SAME FfiRequest goes out each attempt - the replay is matched on the k1 set, h,
h2 and amount, so a fresh secret would make it a different mutation and a
second real burn.

## CRITICAL: what a service owes a note (LUD-25 Part 2)

A reference mint with a signer returns a raw Part 1 signature for a legacy hash
output. The tolerant default verifies that signature when present but also
admits its omission by a no-signer mint. A cp1 output is owed its cs1 in sig
(sig2 for a split's change) ALWAYS, whatever the options; without it the
outcome is MutationOutcome.Unverifiable.
That means the mutation LANDED, so the note is REAL - persist newSecrets (empty
from a *WithHash call: the caller holds that key) before anything else.
fetchNoteInfo throws for a withdrawRequest with no valid mintPubkey.

LnurlcashClient(requireSignatures = true) also demands the old Part 1 sig over
a hash output (default false). LnurlcashClient(requireMintPubkey = false)
admits a Part 1-only service publishing no mintPubkey (default true). Want a
note a recipient can check offline? Hold a cp1 note.

## API

val client = LnurlcashClient(timeout, http, offline, secretSource,
    requireSignatures = false, requireMintPubkey = true, mutationRetries = 1)

suspend fetchNoteInfo(url): NoteInfo               // maxWithdrawableMsat is authoritative
suspend rotate(callback, k1): MutationOutcome<RotatedNote>
suspend split(callback, k1s, amountMsat): MutationOutcome<SplitNotes>
suspend merge(callback, k1s): MutationOutcome<RotatedNote>
suspend melt(callback, k1, invoice): MutationOutcome<MeltReceipt>
suspend settleNote(baseUrl, k1, expectedAmountMsat, signature): SettledNote
suspend probeBurnedNote(url): NoteFate             // LIVE | GONE | UNKNOWN
suspend fetchPayRequest / requestInvoice / fetchInvoiceStatus / fetchMintAddress
suspend requestMintInvoice(payCallback, amountMsat, mintSecret): Invoice
suspend rotateWithHash(callback, k1, h): MutationOutcome<HashedNote>
suspend splitWithHash(callback, k1s, amountMsat, h, h2): MutationOutcome<HashedSplitNotes>
suspend mergeWithHash(callback, k1s, h): MutationOutcome<HashedNote>
suspend requestMintInvoiceWithHash(payCallback, amountMsat, h): Invoice
  The *WithHash forms take an output the caller already holds: a hash, or a
  Part 2 cp1. They never see the secret behind it, so Unknown/Unverifiable
  carry NO secrets from them: persist it BEFORE the call.

Top-level pure functions: verifyNoteSignature, verifyNoteSignatureHash,
generateNoteSecret, hashK1, isPreimage, resolveNoteInput, resolveMintInput,
resolveLnurlInput, isAllowedServiceUrl, buildNoteUrl, withNewK1, withoutK1,
noteK1, noteDeclaredAmountMsat, noteSignature, buildNoteInfoUrlByHash,
parseMintFee, applyMintFee, grossUpForMintFee, describeMintFee,
decodeBolt11AmountMsat, isBolt11Invoice, sameInvoice.

Seed derivation (nodes are privateKey || chainCode, 128 hex chars):
deriveCashRoot(seedHex), deriveCashDomainNode(root, host), cashDomainIndices(root, host),
deriveCashMaster(seedHex), deriveCashChild(node, index: UInt) (hardened iff
index >= 2^31). Part 1 secrets are plain randomness, not seed-derived.
LEGACY, do not mint under: deriveNoteRoot, deriveNoteSecret.

Amounts are Long milli-satoshis everywhere (the bindings' ULong is converted).

## LUD-25 Part 2: a note keyed by a public key, spent by a BIP-340 Schnorr proof

Hex in, hex out, as everywhere else here. Decoders return null, never throw.
encodeCp1/decodeCp1/isCp1   note pubkey, 32-byte x-only, bech32m "cp"
encodeCk1/decodeCk1/isCk1   bearer secret, 96-byte x-only pk||Schnorr sig, "ck". SPENDS
  decode/is also accept the legacy 65-byte recoverable-ECDSA shape so an old
  note can be rotated; encode only takes the current 96 bytes
encodeCs1WithAmount/decodeCs1WithAmount/isCs1WithAmount
  current mint certificate, Cs1(amountMsat, signature); HRP is "cs" plus the
  BOLT11 amount suffix. Signature covers LNURLcash:<amount_msat>:<hex(pk)>.
encodeCs1/decodeCs1/isCs1   LEGACY fixed "cs" HRP only
decodeAnyCs1/isAnyCs1       migration helpers accepting either certificate
encodeCx1/decodeCx1/isCx1   watch-only branch, Cx1(pubkeyXOnly, chainCode), "cx"
  No length limit; all-uppercase accepted; mixed case, a bech32 (not
  bech32m) checksum, the wrong hrp or length and non-zero padding refused
deriveCashAddressNode(root, host)   m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, hashing key m/139'/0:
  the spec's literal path, the same node deriveCashDomainNode returns. Bearer
  material
cashNodeToCx1(node): Cx1   the part to hand out; it links every note on the
  branch but spends none
deriveNotePubkey(P, chainCode, i: UInt)   watch-only; i any UInt, never
  hardened. t >= n is an error, never reduced: use the next index
deriveNoteSecretKey(p, chainCode, i: UInt)   negates p first when P has odd y
Java: both note derivation functions also accept a long index in 0..4294967295;
out-of-range indices throw IllegalArgumentException. Kotlin UInt overloads remain.
signNoteOwnership(sk) -> 96-byte hex   pk||BIP-340 sig over sha256("LNURLcash"),
  zero auxiliary input so seed recovery reproduces the ck1. encodeCk1 it for
  the wire
signAddressProof(indexZeroSk, action, username) -> 64-byte hex
  reference address register/update/unregister proof; BIP-340 over
  sha256("LNURLcash:<register|unregister>:<normalised username>")
recoverNoteOwnershipPubkey(payload) -> pk?   verifies against the sha256
  digest, then the pre-2026-09-16 raw message, before returning the key
noteIdOf(k1) -> id?   sha256(k1) for a secret, the verified embedded key for a
  ck1. Compare notes by this, never by k1
noteLookupOf(k1) -> String?   the hash, or the cp1 for a ck1; pass it to
  buildNoteInfoUrlByHash, which sends a cp1 as p and a hash as h
verifyNoteSignature also takes a ck1 as k1 and a cs1 as the signature;
  verifyNoteSignatureHash(id, amountMsat, sig, mintPubkey) checks by pk or hash
Wire: a ck1 goes wherever a k1 does; a cp1 wherever an output does.
  requestMintInvoiceWithHash: a cp1 goes as the comment alone (a hash also
  sends h). rotate/split/mergeWithHash: p1/p2 for a cp1, h/h2 for a hash.
  fetchNoteInfo compares an echoed ck1 by its verified note id; another key
  is refused
deriveNostrCashSeed(sk) / deriveNostrAddressNode(sk, host)   NOT LUD-25: a
  branch from a Nostr identity key, via
  HMAC-SHA256(key = sk, msg = "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"), then the address path

## MutationOutcome

Mutations RETURN this; they do not throw. The dangerous case is not an error,
it is an unknown.

MutationOutcome.Confirmed(value)                    the service confirmed it
MutationOutcome.Rejected(error)                     definitive: it did not happen
MutationOutcome.Unknown(newSecrets, message, cause) MAYBE - persist newSecrets
                                                    FIRST, then probeBurnedNote
MutationOutcome.Unverifiable(newSecrets, message)   it LANDED, and a cp1 output
                                                    came back with no cs1 (or a
                                                    legacy hash omitted sig under
                                                    requireSignatures). The note
                                                    is REAL - persist newSecrets

getOrThrow() collapses Unknown and Unverifiable into an exception and loses the
secrets. Only use it where losing the note would not matter.

## Rules

1. maxWithdrawableMsat is the ONLY authoritative value; a note URL's amount is a claim.
2. The wallet generates replacement secrets; never accept a service-supplied k1.
3. On Unknown: save newSecrets, then probeBurnedNote.
4. A melt's Confirmed means IN FLIGHT. NotePending means retry, not spent.
5. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note.
6. Never log note URLs - the secret is in the query string. A ck1 is a secret
   too; a cp1, cs1 and cx1 are not, but a cx1 links every note on its branch.
7. Compare notes by noteIdOf, never by the k1 string.

## Conformance

https://github.com/lnurlcash/lnurlcash-conformance
